title: PORTABLE SINGER CASED ELECTRIC...
reason: Singer 222K free arm Featherweight with case, controller and accessories, sold only as a portable Singer; these commonly make several hundred dollars when working (my guess $300 to $700).
findings: Singer Featherweight 222K, the free arm model (not the common 221), made at Kilbowie in Scotland roughly 1953 to 1964. The gold oval Singer medallion with a clear 222K cartouche is on the pillar, the SINGER decal is on the arm, and a small stamp left of the badge ends '...BRITAIN' (made in Great Britain, only partly legible). Serial number not visible in the photos. Maker claim (Singer) is supported but the title never gives the 222K model, so it is under-described. Comes in its black carry case with a black foot controller and lead (modern looking black flex with an Australian 3 pin plug), a tan accessory box, a small box of presser feet and attachments, a white box with two metal rings, a rolled instruction booklet and a red tray of thread, pins and buttons.
condition: Machine looks glossy with decals mostly intact and only light bed and base wear; case is scuffed with a worn lining; cord and plug are not original age and motor wiring would need testing and tagging; sold as going order by the auctioneer; some original accessories may be missing; serial and run condition unchecked.
rescore_note: The 222K badge is clearly visible, so this is a genuine Kilbowie free-arm Featherweight (a better model than the common 221), glossy with case, controller and accessories; held back by an untested motor, a replaced lead and an unseen serial; about $300 to $500. Estimate only, no comparable sales checked (search budget used up).
